title: Security lane harness and declared-boundary roster
description:
Objective: build the enumeration artifact the Security fault matrix (task-05ce9b8f982f448a9cdaa4142a653f32) needs before any hostile coverage can be claimed complete. Foundation slice of the SPIDR re-slice.

MEASURED, BY LISTING NOT GUESSING (HEAD abc3dcf). The repo declares its authority and external-effect boundaries as exported layer constants. `grep -rn "^export const [A-Z_]*\(LAYERS\|LAYER\|BOUNDARIES\) = " --include=*.ts apps packages adapters | grep -v node_modules | grep -v '\.test\.'` returns EXACTLY 85, distributed: apps/daemon 32, packages/runner 18, packages/core 10, packages/scheduler 7, packages/store 4, apps/control-room 4, packages/contracts 3, adapters/ide-contract 2, and one each in review, mcp, import, coordination, control-room-client. That 85-member set IS the whole-system enumeration DoD 1 of the parent demands, and it is why the parent cannot be one task.

Deliverable, two parts:
1. A HAND-WRITTEN roster in tests/security naming all 85 constants with their declaring file, plus a source scan, asserted set-equal in BOTH directions. Hand-written AND compared is deliberate: a table derived from the scan cannot police the scan, and a hand list alone silently under-covers the day a 86th boundary lands. Each entry also carries a coverage-axis tag (transport / integrity / durable-store / runtime-provider / scheduler-activation) so the sibling slices can claim their subset without overlap or gap.
2. A hostile-probe harness the sibling slices consume: bounded before/after/race drivers, per-case temp roots with guaranteed cleanup, and a refusal assertion helper that pins BOTH the stable reason code AND the answering layer constant.

THE RATCHET IS DELIBERATELY OPEN HERE. This task asserts only that the roster matches the source exactly and that every axis tag is used at least once. It does NOT yet assert that every boundary has hostile coverage — task-05ce's final gate slice closes that. Do not close it early; a ratchet closed before the coverage exists just blocks its own siblings.

NOT in scope: any hostile coverage of a specific boundary, corpus bytes, campaign scoring, claim decisions, or anything under tests/fault/**.

Owned paths: tests/security/boundary-roster.security.ts, tests/security/hostile-harness.ts. Do not modify tests/security/vitest.config.ts, tsconfig.json or lane-smoke.security.ts.

Verification: `pnpm test:security` — read the OUTPUT. The lane already typechecks first (`tsc -p tests/security/tsconfig.json && vitest run --config tests/security/vitest.config.ts`) and sets passWithNoTests:false, but exit 0 is still not evidence: require a printed Test Files/Tests count line above the current lane-smoke-only baseline.
definitionOfDone: The roster is HAND-WRITTEN, names all 85 declared boundary constants with their declaring file path, and is asserted set-equal against a live source scan in BOTH directions — a constant added to the source with no roster entry reddens, and a roster entry with no source constant reddens.

The roster asserts an exact cardinality of 85 and asserts the per-area distribution (apps/daemon 32, packages/runner 18, packages/core 10, packages/scheduler 7, packages/store 4, apps/control-room 4, packages/contracts 3, adapters/ide-contract 2, review/mcp/import/coordination/control-room-client 1 each), so a scan that silently matches zero or half cannot pass.

Every roster entry carries exactly one axis tag from the closed set {transport, integrity, durable-store, runtime-provider, scheduler-activation}, every tag is used at least once, and no constant carries two tags — asserted, so the sibling slices partition the set with no overlap and no gap.

The hostile harness exposes bounded before/after/race drivers and a refusal helper that pins BOTH reason code AND answering layer; a test proves the helper FAILS when given only a code, so it cannot be used to write a layer-blind assertion.
A mutation renaming one declared boundary constant in its source file turns a NAMED roster test red, proving the scan reads real source rather than a cached list.
`pnpm test:security` runs with its exit code captured separately (never `;`-chained, never piped into tail) and prints a Test Files/Tests count line strictly above the lane-smoke-only baseline.
taskRails: The roster is hand-written AND source-compared, both directions. A generated table cannot police its own generator, and a hand list alone under-covers silently.
Do NOT close the completeness ratchet in this task. Asserting that every boundary has hostile coverage before the sibling slices land would block them; the final gate slice owns that flip.
The harness contains NO authority: it drives probes and asserts refusals, it never decides whether a boundary refused correctly. Every verdict comes from the production surface under test.

Preserve foreign work; commit only the explicit owned paths by pathspec. Do not touch tests/fault/** — tests/fault/disaster-restore/** belongs to task-0c89476b78044024b07c86c0c8986bd0 and other fault subtrees have their own owners.

implementationPlan.description:
TDD RED — write the roster's own assertions before the roster. Create `tests/security/boundary-roster.security.ts` and let it fail on the missing hand-written table. The tests to pin, in this order because each catches a different way the roster can go quietly wrong:
(a) CARDINALITY: the hand-written roster holds exactly 87 entries. A bare set-equality passes vacuously if BOTH sides are empty; the literal count is what stops that.
(b) PER-AREA DISTRIBUTION: assert the nine-way split above by counting roster entries per top-level package. A scanner that silently matched only one directory satisfies set-equality against a roster built from the same broken scan; distribution catches it.
(c) BIDIRECTIONAL SET-EQUALITY against a LIVE source scan — roster-minus-scan and scan-minus-roster both empty, each failure naming the offending constant AND its file, never just a count.
(d) AXIS PARTITION: every entry carries exactly one tag from the closed set {transport, integrity, durable-store, runtime-provider, scheduler-activation}; every tag used at least once; no entry tagged twice; the five tag-groups sum to 87.
(e) THE EXCLUSION RULE IS TESTED, not just documented: assert that the scanner does NOT return `EXPECTED_REFUSAL_LAYERS` from project-configuration.test-fixtures.ts and does NOT return `CORE_FAULT_BOUNDARIES` from packages/testkit — named explicitly, so a future loosening of the filter reddens here instead of silently inflating the roster.
(f) THE ANNOTATED FORM IS MATCHED: assert the scanner DOES return `PLATFORM_LINUX_LAYER` and `PLATFORM_MACOS_LAYER`, the two that a ` = `-only pattern misses. This is the regression test for the exact defect this step corrects.
implementationPlan.note:
TDD RED — assertions written before the roster and the scanner. Gate run: `pnpm test:security`, EXIT=1, `Test Files 1 failed | 1 passed (2)`, `Tests 12 failed | 23 passed (35)`.

THE RED IS ASSERTION FAILURE, NOT A COMPILE ERROR. `tsc -p tests/security/tsconfig.json` passed — the lane runs tsc first and `&&`-gates vitest on it, so vitest executing at all proves the file typechecks. That matters: a compile-error RED would have told me nothing about which assertions work, and I would not have seen the vacuity finding below. I removed `readdirSync`/`readFileSync`/`relative` from the import line to get here — `tsconfig.base.json` sets `noUnusedLocals: true`, so importing step 3's dependencies early would have failed the build instead of the tests. They go back in with the scanner.

STUB CHOICE, deliberate: `scanDeclaredBoundaries()` THROWS rather than returning `[]`. An empty-array stub would have made the two exclusion cases (e) and the non-empty-scan case pass vacuously — "does not return EXPECTED_REFUSAL_LAYERS" is trivially true of a scanner that returns nothing. Throwing guarantees no scan-dependent assertion can report a false green during the RED phase. All 8 scan-dependent tests failed with `scanDeclaredBoundaries not implemented`.

THE 12 FAILURES, each for its intended reason:
- cardinality: `expected [] to have a length of 87 but got +0`
- distribution: `expected {} to deeply equal { 'apps/daemon': 32, …(12) }`
- 8x scan-dependent: `Error: scanDeclaredBoundaries not implemented`
- axis coverage: all five axes reported unused
- axis partition sum: `expected +0 to be 87`

MEASURED VACUITY — the plan predicted this and the RED run demonstrates it concretely. Six of my file's tests PASSED against an empty roster:
- "has no duplicate entries" — 0 keys, 0 unique, passes
- "tags every entry with exactly one axis" — nothing to violate
- "assigns each constant to exactly one axis" — nothing to violate
- "sums the per-area distribution to the roster size" — pure arithmetic over my constants
- "classifies the four exclusion shapes..." — pure predicate, genuinely correct already
- "matches the annotated form directly against the pattern" — pure regex, genuinely correct already
The first three are exactly the vacuous-on-empty shape the plan warned about, and CARDINALITY + DISTRIBUTION + AXIS-COVERAGE are what make an empty roster unrepresentable. That is the argument for those three assertions, now demonstrated rather than asserted.

TWO ASSERTIONS THAT ARE ALREADY GREEN AND ARE MEANT TO BE — both are pure unit checks with no dependency on roster data, so they carry real signal from the first run:
- the predicate case pins all four exclusion shapes AND one ordinary production module (`goal-results.ts` -> true), so the rule cannot be satisfied by a predicate that rejects everything.
- the pattern case pins the annotated form `A_LAYER: PlatformLayer =` -> "A_LAYER", the plain form `B_LAYERS =` -> "B_LAYERS", AND two negatives: a doc-comment line ` * export const C_LAYER = ...` -> null (prose cannot match, because the pattern is anchored at column 0) and `NOT_A_BOUNDARY` -> null (the name must end in LAYER/LAYERS/BOUNDARIES). Those two negatives are the regression test for the two scanner failure modes recorded in Serena: a whole-contents scan that matches prose, and a bare-prefix anchor.

INDEPENDENT ARITHMETIC CHECK, free from the sum test: EXPECTED_DISTRIBUTION's thirteen values sum to exactly 87, verified by the green "sums the per-area distribution to the roster size". So the nine-way split I encoded is internally consistent with the cardinality before any roster entry exists.

DESIGN NOTES for what follows:
- entries are keyed `constant@file`, not by name alone, so every set-difference failure names the constant AND its declaring file rather than a count. All 87 names are in fact unique (measured in step 1), so this is defence against a future collision, not a present one.
- `findRepoRoot()` walks upward searching for `pnpm-workspace.yaml` and throws if it reaches the filesystem root. No `../..` hop-count anywhere in the file.
- `DECLARATION_PATTERN` is line-anchored at column 0, carries the optional `(?::[^=]+)?` annotation group, and terminates on `=`.
- the coverage ratchet is OPEN: nothing in this file asserts that any boundary has hostile coverage. The header says so explicitly and names task-3b1cbdf9bd39405bb32230552d3ab242 as the owner of that flip.

Roster and scanner bodies are still stubs; step 3 fills both.

implementationPlan.description:
WRITE THE ROSTER AND THE SCANNER. The roster is a frozen hand-written array of 87 `{constant, file, axis}` records. Hand-written AND source-compared is the whole design: a table derived from the scan cannot police the scan, and a hand list alone under-covers silently the day an 88th boundary lands. Type the `axis` field against the closed five-member union so a typo is a compile error rather than an orphaned tag.
THE SCANNER MUST FIND THE REPO ROOT BY SEARCHING, NEVER BY HOP-COUNTING. Walk upward from `dirname(fileURLToPath(import.meta.url))` looking for `pnpm-workspace.yaml` — the same technique `packages/runner/src/platform/windows/windows-broker-path.ts` uses and documents as "searched for, never hop-counted". A `../../..` join silently narrows the scan root when a file moves, and a scan rooted one directory too deep returns fewer constants while the roster still matches whatever it found.
Scan `apps/`, `packages/` and `adapters/` for `.ts` files, skipping `node_modules` and every test-support path named in step 1's exclusion rule, and match `^export const ([A-Z_]+(?:LAYERS|LAYER|BOUNDARIES))\s*(?::[^=]+)?=` per line — the optional annotation group is what the original count missed. Return `{constant, file}` with the file relative to the repo root so roster entries and scan results compare as plain strings.
Assert the scan itself found something before comparing: a scan returning zero satisfies set-equality against an empty roster, and (a) plus (b) from step 2 are what make that impossible.

implementationPlan.description:
BUILD THE HOSTILE HARNESS the five sibling slices consume. Create `tests/security/hostile-harness.ts`. Note it is NOT a `.security.ts` file, so the lane will not execute it as a suite — it is imported. Provide:
(1) BEFORE / AFTER / RACE drivers, each BOUNDED and each guaranteed to terminate. The failure mode these guard against is a hang, and a hanging test reports no verdict at all rather than a red one — so every driver takes an explicit bound and fails loudly when it expires rather than waiting.
(2) Per-case temp roots under `os.tmpdir()` with a registry and a cleanup that removes every root on every exit path including throws. The lane runs `fileParallelism: false`, so one leaked root or held handle stalls everything after it.
(3) A REFUSAL ASSERTION HELPER that requires BOTH the stable reason code AND the answering layer constant. Make the layer parameter non-optional so a layer-blind assertion does not compile, and add a case in the roster file proving the helper REJECTS a call carrying only a code — a helper that permits the weak form will be used in the weak form by five sibling slices.
THE HARNESS HOLDS NO AUTHORITY. It drives probes and asserts; it never decides whether a boundary refused correctly, never reimplements a codec, a digest or an admission rule. Every verdict comes from the production surface under test. Keep it under 250 physical lines by `grep -c ''` (PowerShell `Measure-Object -Line` undercounts); if it would exceed, that is a signal it has grown authority it should not have.

Per the board rail I did not amend, reset, or re-claim those commits. I re-verified the deliverable from disk rather than trusting the dead session's claims.

WHAT I CHANGED THIS SESSION: the harness was 279 physical lines, over this step's 250 cap. I compressed prose only — no export removed, no behaviour changed, no authority added or dropped. Now 248 by `grep -c ''` (PowerShell Measure-Object undercounts, so grep is the measure). The only code-shape change: `requireBound` merged its two numeric guards into one range check `!Number.isInteger || <=0 || > MAX_BOUND_MS`; both arms still throw HostileHarnessMisuseError, and the roster's "refuses a bound above MAX_BOUND_MS instead of letting setTimeout clamp it to 1ms" case still passes. `readRefusal` now returns `RefusalExpectation` instead of a duplicate `ObservedRefusal` interface of identical shape.

WHAT THE HARNESS PROVIDES (all three parts of the step):
(1) BOUNDED DRIVERS. probeBefore (probe then effect), probeAfter (effect then probe), probeRacing (concurrent, records `firstSettled`). Every leg goes through `withBound`, which races real work against a timer and ALWAYS clears it in `finally`. Expiry throws HostileBoundExceededError naming the stalled label — a distinct class, so a bound breach can never be misread as a refusal. MAX_BOUND_MS = 2_147_483_647 is refused rather than clamped: setTimeout clamps a wider delay to 1ms, so a caller widening a bound "to be safe" would silently get the TIGHTEST bound instead of the loosest.
   probeRacing REPORTS both legs as LegOutcome rather than propagating the first rejection: in hostile probing the refusing leg is usually the interesting one, and propagating would discard the other leg AND destroy the settle order, which is the single fact the driver exists to establish.
(2) TEMP ROOTS. hostileRoot(label) mkdtemps under os.tmpdir() and registers the root; cleanupHostileRoots() removes every registered root and never throws (a throw on one root would skip the rest and leak them all); withHostileRoot removes its root in `finally`, so the throwing path cleans too — asserted by the roster case "removes a temp root on the throwing exit path". Roots are realpath'd because macOS tmpdir() is the /var -> /private/var symlink and a containment check on the unresolved form reads a legitimate root as a path escape.
(3) REFUSAL HELPER. assertRefusedWith(actual, {code, layer}) with `layer` NON-OPTIONAL, guarded twice: the type makes a code-only call a compile error, and a runtime check rejects one arriving through a cast. Roster proves the weak form is rejected — "REJECTS an expectation carrying only a code" casts `{code}` to RefusalExpectation and expects HostileHarnessMisuseError. Mismatches are distinguished: /refusal code mismatch/ vs /refusal layer mismatch/, so a test cannot pass on the code while a different layer answered.

NO AUTHORITY, per the task rail: the harness never decides whether a boundary was right to refuse, never derives an expected code or layer, and reimplements no codec, digest or admission rule. Every expected value is supplied by the caller; every verdict comes from the production surface under test.

1) Keep the filed 85 and let the siblings' counts stand. REJECTED once measured: 85 omits two real platform boundaries, so the ratchet child would later demand coverage for constants no sibling was told to cover, and the gap would surface as a late red with no obvious owner. Correcting it here, in the roster that is declared authoritative, is the cheapest possible moment.

2) Take the loose pattern's 89 as-is. REJECTED: it admits a test fixture and a testkit name-table. A roster inflated with test-support entries would demand hostile coverage for things that are not boundaries, which is worse than under-counting because it cannot be satisfied honestly.

3) Generate the roster from the scan. REJECTED — it is the defining mistake for this artifact: a generated table cannot police its own generator, and the scan is exactly what needs policing (this task exists because a scan pattern was wrong). Hand-written plus bidirectional comparison is the only form that catches a bad scanner.

4) Assert set-equality only, without cardinality or distribution. REJECTED: set-equality between an empty scan and an empty roster passes, and a scan narrowed to one directory passes against a roster built from that same narrow scan. The literal 87 and the nine-way split are what make those unrepresentable, and drill 3 proves it.

5) Close the coverage ratchet here so the roster is "complete" in one task. REJECTED and explicitly forbidden by this task's rails: no sibling has landed coverage yet, so the assertion would fail permanently and block the five slices that are supposed to satisfy it. task-3b1cbdf9 owns the flip.

6) Put the harness in a `.security.ts` file. REJECTED: the lane executes every `*.security.ts`, so a harness with that suffix becomes a suite with no cases — and `passWithNoTests: false` would then make its emptiness a lane failure rather than a helpful one.
planningNotes.codebaseInsights:
MEASURED AT HEAD abc3dcf. I filed this task and its five siblings from a boundary enumeration I ran during the SPIDR re-slice. PLANNING IT REVEALED A DEFECT IN MY OWN COUNT, and correcting it is step 1's job.

THE MISCOUNT. I enumerated with `grep -rn "^export const [A-Z_]*\(LAYERS\|LAYER\|BOUNDARIES\) = "`, which demands ` = ` immediately after the name and so misses every constant with a type annotation. Strict pattern: 85. Loose pattern allowing `: Type =`: 89. The four-constant delta:
- packages/runner/src/platform/linux-facts.ts:41 `PLATFORM_LINUX_LAYER: PlatformLayer` — REAL BOUNDARY, include.
- packages/runner/src/platform/macos/macos-facts.ts:45 `PLATFORM_MACOS_LAYER: PlatformLayer` — REAL BOUNDARY, include.
- packages/contracts/src/configuration/project-configuration.test-fixtures.ts:42 `EXPECTED_REFUSAL_LAYERS` — EXCLUDE, a test fixture. It evaded `grep -v '\.test\.'` because `.test-fixtures.ts` contains no `.test.` segment — a filter gap worth knowing.
- packages/testkit/src/schedule/schedule-universe-tables.ts:171 `CORE_FAULT_BOUNDARIES` — EXCLUDE, @moe/testkit is test-support and this LISTS boundary names rather than declaring one.
CORRECTED ROSTER SIZE: 87. Distribution: apps/daemon 32, packages/runner 20, packages/core 10, packages/scheduler 7, packages/store 4, apps/control-room 4, packages/contracts 3, adapters/ide-contract 2, one each in review/mcp/import/coordination/control-room-client. 32+20+10+7+4+4+3+2+5 = 87.

CONSEQUENCE FOR THE SIBLINGS: their filed subset counts (transport 13, integrity 18, durable-store 8, runtime-provider 20, scheduler-activation 16) were derived from the old 85. runtime-provider gains the two platform constants and becomes 22. Every sibling was told to "consume the roster's axis tag as the definitive subset", so the roster overrides their filed counts — but the completion must say so explicitly or a sibling worker will trust their own description.

THE EXCLUSION RULE, which is the roster's real contract: a declared boundary is a constant a PRODUCTION module exports to name a refusal layer. Test-support files (`*.test.ts`, `*.test-fixtures.ts`, `*-fixtures.ts`, anything under packages/testkit) and constants that merely LIST other boundaries' names are not declarations.

LANE FACTS (tests/security/vitest.config.ts): `root` is the lane dir; includes only `**/*.security.ts`; excludes `*.fault.ts`/`*.test.ts`/`*.spec.ts` so a file cannot run in both lanes; `passWithNoTests: false`; `retry: 0`; `allowOnly: false`; `fileParallelism: false`; `maxConcurrency: 1`; locale-independent sequencer. `pnpm test:security` runs `tsc -p tests/security/tsconfig.json` FIRST, so the whole lane typechecks before anything executes. The tsconfig extends tsconfig.base.json with `types: ["node"]` and includes `./**/*.ts`.

PRECEDENT TO COPY: `tests/security/lane-smoke.security.ts` (251 lines) already reads files with `readFileSync` and imports the three vitest configs to certify lane discovery — so a source-scanning security case is an established pattern here, not a novelty. `hostile-harness.ts` deliberately has no `.security.ts` suffix, so the lane imports it without executing it as a suite.

ROOT-FINDING PRECEDENT: `packages/runner/src/platform/windows/windows-broker-path.ts` documents "The file that marks the workspace root. Searched for, never hop-counted" and searches for `pnpm-workspace.yaml`. The scanner must do the same; an `import.meta.url` hop-count silently narrows the scan root.
planningNotes.risks:
1) THE COUNT IN THIS TASK'S OWN DESCRIPTION IS WRONG. It says 85; the answer is 87. A worker who trusts the description will build a roster that fails its own bidirectional comparison against a correct scanner, or worse, will "fix" the scanner to match 85 and re-introduce the annotation blind spot. Step 1 exists to make the correction the first thing that happens.

2) A SILENTLY NARROWED SCAN PASSES SET-EQUALITY. If the scanner roots one directory too deep, it returns fewer constants — and if the roster was built from that same scan, both sides agree. Cardinality plus per-area distribution are the guards; drill 3 proves they work. Find the root by SEARCHING for pnpm-workspace.yaml, never by hop-counting.

3) THE `.test-fixtures.ts` FILTER GAP is subtle and will recur: `grep -v '\.test\.'` does not exclude `.test-fixtures.ts`. Encode the exclusion rule in the scanner and assert the two excluded constants BY NAME, so a future filter loosening reddens instead of inflating the roster.

4) A HELPER THAT PERMITS THE WEAK FORM WILL BE USED IN THE WEAK FORM. Five sibling slices consume the refusal helper. If the layer parameter is optional, layer-blind assertions will appear across all five and every one of them detaches the moment a different layer starts answering. Make it non-optional and prove the weak form is rejected.

5) DO NOT CLOSE THE RATCHET. Asserting full hostile coverage here blocks the five siblings that are meant to provide it.

6) HANGS REPORT NO VERDICT. The lane runs `fileParallelism: false`, so one unbounded driver or leaked handle stalls everything after it. Every driver bounded, every temp root cleaned on every exit path including throws.

7) DRILL 1 EDITS A PRODUCTION FILE in a shared worktree. Revert via `git checkout --` and confirm clean before moving on — a foreign whole-tree completion hook can commit a drill left on disk, which has already happened twice on this board.

8) EXIT 0 IS NOT EVIDENCE. `passWithNoTests: false` catches a fully empty lane, but a lane collecting only lane-smoke still exits 0. Require the count line above the baseline.

9) THE SIBLINGS' FILED COUNTS ARE NOW STALE. Say so in the completion: runtime-provider becomes 22, and the roster's axis tags are the authority every sibling was told to consume.
